name: NVIDIA GTC 2026 News Roundup

announcements.name: NVIDIA OpenShell
announcements.what: Open-source agent sandbox runtime with kernel-level isolation, policy engine, privacy router

announcements.name: NVIDIA NemoClaw
announcements.what: OpenClaw + OpenShell + Nemotron bundle for secure autonomous agents

announcements.name: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit / AI-Q
announcements.what: Python framework for building multi-agent workflows with MCP/A2A support
announcements.notes: Python-only, enterprise-focused, not applicable to our CLI+tmux stack

announcements.name: NVIDIA cuOpt
announcements.notes: Logistics optimization, not software agent orchestration

announcements.name: Vera Rubin Platform
announcements.what: Full-stack computing platform for agentic AI (7 chips, 5 rack systems)

announcements.name: DGX Spark / DGX Station
announcements.what: Desktop/deskside AI supercomputers for local model inference
announcements.notes: Interesting for local model hosting but we use Claude Max subscriptions

announcements.name: Nemotron 3
announcements.what: Frontier open model family for language, reasoning, speech, vision
announcements.notes: Open model alternative, but we use Claude/GPT via subscriptions

announcements.name: OpenClaw
announcements.what: Open-source autonomous agent framework (100K+ GitHub stars)
announcements.notes: Primarily robotics/embodied AI focused, but 100K stars signals massive community

summary: GTC 2026 is overwhelmingly hardware + robotics + enterprise. The only items relevant to our coding agent orchestrator are OpenShell (sandbox runtime, 7/10) and NemoClaw (the bundled deployment, 7/10). Everything else targets enterprise GPU pipelines, physical AI, or logistics — not CLI-based coding agents. AI-Q is a WATCH for MCP/A2A protocol convergence signals.
